title: Silver Talisman Transmission
next_chapter_hook: When the symbol resembling the patterns of the Tianji Record was seared into Chen Ji's palm, he suddenly realized—the mysterious benefactor's layout had perhaps begun long ago.

text.content: The night was as dark as ink. In the thatched cottage at the Tianqing Sect Back Mountain, Chen Ji sat alone beneath the dim lamplight. The silver talisman in his tightly gripped hand still carried a faint coolness. He stared at the barely visible characters on the talisman's surface, his eyes gleaming with sharp light. Chen Nian's words still echoed in his ears—"Who am I"—these four characters were like blades, repeatedly gouging at his heart. His sister, who had been missing for years, suddenly appeared, yet at a crucial moment asked such a question. There must be something suspicious here. He drew the silver talisman closer to the lamp, attempting to find more clues from the mottled rune marks. Suddenly, a burning heat came from his fingertips—the silver talisman lit up on its own.

Silver light burst forth, illuminating the entire thatched cottage as bright as day. Chen Ji instinctively activated his spiritual energy for protection, yet the light carried no hint of attack. Instead, it bore a familiar warmth—exactly the same sensation as when he first received the silver talisman warning months ago. The light flowed across the talisman's surface, gradually coalescing into rows of tiny characters, each word swimming and flickering like fish on the silver surface.

dialogue.content: "On the day of the ceremony, great change will come. Not your fault, but Heaven's will."

text.content: Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply. The origin of this silver talisman remained unconfirmed to this day. He only knew that whenever danger loomed, it would appear at the appropriate time, providing warnings. However, this time, the content within the runes differed greatly from before—Not your fault, but Heaven's will. These eight characters carried far more weight than any substantial warning. The implication was that no matter how he planned, irreversible changes would occur at the ceremony.

He drew a deep breath and continued examining the talisman's surface. As the silver light shifted, the second line of text slowly appeared: "Xuan Dao Sect's destruction was not the work of external enemies, but internal strife. The item your father protected in the past concerns the origin of the Tianji Record. Be cautious, be most cautious."

dialogue.content: "The protected item... concerns the origin of the Tianji Record..."

text.content: Chen Ji's breathing grew rapid. Xuan Dao Sect, the reclusive sect that had been annihilated in a single night thirty years ago—he had not yet been born at that time. Regarding its destruction, the world's prevailing account was a large-scale invasion by the Demonic Path, yet the silver talisman's account was entirely different—internal strife. What level of internal betrayal could cause a sect that had inherited traditions for thousands of years to collapse in one night? And how had his father become connected to such a force?

choice.prompt: The information on the silver talisman plunged Chen Ji into deep thought—regarding his father's past and the origin of the Tianji Record, he needed to make a choice.

choices.description: Since Xuan Dao Sect has been destroyed, there must be remaining clues. Perhaps I can find his father's connection to this force.
choices.visible_reward: Obtain clues about Xuan Dao Sect
choices.risk_hint: Investigation may attract the attention of those with ulterior motives

text.content: Chen Ji rose, retrieving a yellowed booklet from a hidden compartment beneath his bed—this was a compilation of intelligence from various sources he had gathered over many years. The records regarding Xuan Dao Sect were few, but enough to prove this sect was extraordinary. He closed his eyes, his mind racing, and began tracing clues through his father's network of relationships during his lifetime.

choices.description: Since the Tianji Record is connected to what his father protected, perhaps more clues can be found within the fragments.
choices.visible_reward: Unlock partial truth of the Tianji Record
choices.risk_hint: Using the Tianji Record will consume precious Heavenly Fate

text.content: Chen Ji tucked the silver talisman into his chest and turned toward the secret chamber. Taking out that scroll of the broken Tianji Record, he slowly infused it with spiritual energy. The patterns on the fragment lit up once more, and a blurry image flooded into his mind—the back view of a middle-aged man, handing something to a fuzzy silhouette.

choices.description: As the soul guardian of the Tianji Record fragments, Mo Xiansheng may know more details.
choices.risk_hint: Mo Xiansheng only reveals partial truths each time

dialogue.content: The first page of the Tianji Record glowed faintly, and Mo Xiansheng's aged voice sounded: "You came faster than I anticipated. Very well, since you've come this far, there are indeed some things I should let you know."

text.content: Regardless of his choice, the text on the silver talisman continued to appear. The third line of characters emerged especially slowly, as if deliberately waiting for his gaze: "The benefactor's identity, you shall know in time. But before that, three trials must be passed. The ceremony, the blood moon, the forbidden grounds—pass each trial, and you shall glimpse one more truth."

Chen Ji's gaze turned cold. Three trials. The ceremony was clearly the Tianqing Sect's sect ceremony in three days, when the three major sects would gather, creating a complex situation. The blood moon was a celestial anomaly occurring a month later, when the Demonic Path's power was said to be at its strongest. And the forbidden grounds... A contemplative glint flickered in his eyes. He had once conducted a distant reconnaissance of the forbidden grounds at the Tianqing Sect Back Mountain. The atmosphere there was exceedingly strange, as if hiding some force capable of devouring everything.

Chen Ji sneered. This benefactor certainly had grand airs, setting three trials to test him yet refusing to reveal their true identity. However, on second thought, if the other party had truly laid everything bare without reservation, he would instead suspect a trap. A being capable of transmitting information in such a hidden manner, with such deep scheming and grand gestures, was by no means an ordinary person.

The light on the silver talisman began to fade gradually, as if the transmission was nearing its end. Yet just as Chen Ji thought the information had concluded, the final line of text suddenly blazed brightly, its characters clearer than any previous line, as if deliberately branding itself into his mind: "Your father Chen Xuan died protecting the complete key to the Tianji Record. This key is divided into three pieces, scattered across various places. What I hold is merely one of them."

Chen Ji abruptly stood up. He had long known of the Tianji Record's incompleteness, yet he had never imagined such an astonishing truth lay behind its fragmentation. The Tianji Record was not naturally broken, but had been deliberately divided into several parts. His father, Chen Xuan, had sacrificed his life guarding one of these pieces. The mysterious benefactor held one of the keys—what did this mean?

He forced himself to calm down, beginning to sort through the chaotic thoughts in his mind. He had never truly investigated the cause of his father's death, only knowing the official account was an accident during an outside training excursion. Yet now, it seemed nothing was coincidental. Xuan Dao Sect's destruction, his father's death, the Tianji Record's incompleteness, the benefactor's appearance... These seemingly unrelated events were, it seemed, being manipulated by an invisible hand.

choice.prompt: The silver talisman transmission revealed shocking secrets, and Chen Ji needed to decide his next move.

choices.description: Since the benefactor can传授 such secrets, they must have sincere intentions for cooperation. Perhaps proactively make contact to see what they truly want.
choices.visible_reward: Gain more trust and information from the benefactor
choices.risk_hint: The other party's intentions are unclear; blindly trusting may be a trap

text.content: Chen Ji took out a blank talisman paper, briefly writing his questions and next intentions, then placed it on the windowsill. A moment later, the silver talisman trembled slightly, as if sensing something, and transformed itself into a stream of light that streaked across the sky. He gazed at where the silver light vanished, thinking to himself: Since the other party's scheme runs this deep, they surely will not easily abandon this chess piece of theirs.

choices.description: Regardless of whether the information is true or false, it must first be verified through other channels. The Tianqing Sect's library may have relevant records on Xuan Dao Sect.
choices.visible_cost: Need to take some risk infiltrating the library
choices.visible_reward: Obtain an independent source of intelligence
choices.risk_hint: The library has barriers; forcibly entering may alert the sect

text.content: The Tianqing Sect's library was already open to Servant Disciples. Chen Ji used the excuse of consulting basic martial technique texts, quietly slipping into the forbidden book section. Here were stored many secret files not permitted for ordinary disciples to browse, including scattered records of that great disaster thirty years ago. He quickly found a name—the "Guardian" registry of Xuan Dao Sect, where one entry had been obscured by ink stains, but was still faintly legible: "Chen... Xuan, thirty-seventh generation Key Guardian."

Whether choosing to trust or to verify, Chen Ji had already confirmed one thing—his father's death was by no means accidental; he had sacrificed himself guarding a key part of the Tianji Record. And that mysterious benefactor was most likely his father's former companion or successor, waiting in the shadows for something.

Just as he sank into contemplation, a subtle sound of footsteps suddenly came from outside the window. Chen Ji instantly收敛全身气息, his entire person melting into the shadows. The footsteps stopped at the door of the thatched cottage. After a moment, a familiar voice sounded.

Chen Nian's voice carried a trembling quality, entirely different from that calm and almost cold woman from daytime. Chen Ji remained silent for a moment, yet ultimately opened the door. Chen Nian stood beneath the moonlight, her face deathly pale, her eyes slightly red—she had clearly been crying. Her hand clutched something tightly, and upon seeing Chen Ji, the tears in her eyes could no longer be held back.

dialogue.content: "Brother, I had a dream... I dreamed that you were covered in blood, standing amidst ruins. A voice told me that if I didn't do something, you would die."

text.content: Chen Ji's pupils subtly contracted. Chen Nian's dream—if it were an ordinary nightmare, that would be one thing, but her "Heavenly Fate Lock Key" constitution allowed her dreams to resonate with Heavenly Secrets in some way. This dream might not be a simple nightmare. His gaze fell on Chen Nian's tightly clenched hand, and he slowly spoke.

dialogue.content: "What are you holding in your hand?"

choice.prompt: Chen Nian visited at night, holding something mysterious. Chen Ji needed to respond.

choices.description: Regardless of whether she has something to hide, clearly she is in extreme distress at the moment. As a brother, her emotions should be stabilized first.
choices.visible_cost: May miss the best opportunity to obtain intelligence
choices.risk_hint: The sister's attitude before and after反差过大, credibility questionable

dialogue.content: Chen Ji gently pressed his hand on Chen Nian's shoulder, softly saying: "Come in first. Whatever happened, your brother is here."

choices.description: What she said during the daytime already raised suspicion. Now she visits at night, the前后 attitude反差过大. It must be clarified.
choices.risk_hint: Being too aggressive may push her toward the opposite side

dialogue.content: Chen Ji's gaze abruptly turned cold: "What did you mean by what you said during the daytime? What do you mean I don't know what you're talking about? Chen Nian, you had better tell me everything clearly."

text.content: Upon hearing this, Chen Nian's body trembled slightly. She slowly opened her palm, revealing a small Jade Pendant. The pendant was pure white throughout, with a dark red gem embedded in its center, faintly emitting a soft glow. However, what truly caught Chen Ji's attention was the faintly discernible pattern along the pendant's edge—
That pattern was identical to the runes on the Tianji Record fragments.

dialogue.content: "This... I was holding it in my hand when I woke up. Those people—the people from the Holy Sect—they don't know I have this. I've hidden it well, until today."

text.content: Chen Ji took the Jade Pendant, probing it with his spiritual energy. In an instant, a familiar aura rushed toward him—that was the unique aura of the Tianji Record, yet more pure and complete than on the fragments. His heart surged with waves of shock, yet his expression remained unmoved. Chen Nian's Jade Pendant had a direct connection to the Tianji Record, and might even be a part of the "complete key" mentioned in the silver talisman.

And at that moment, the scene from before the silver talisman's disappearance flashed through Chen Ji's mind once more—a fuzzy symbol flashed in his consciousness, gradually overlapping with the pattern on the Jade Pendant. That symbol, that pattern, that aura... all the clues pointed in the same direction. Chen Ji raised his head, gazing at the sky outside the window that was gradually brightening, and had already formed his plans.

The ceremony in three days seemed to be far more than a simple sect grand event. The benefactor's warning, his father's sacrifice, Chen Nian's origins, the Tianji Record's origin... all of it would converge on that day. And he, Chen Ji, would never allow others to manipulate his fate—regardless of how many decades that figure behind the scenes had been scheming.
